- method static System.Void DownloadParameters(AAMotion.MotionController, System.String, System.Boolean = True, System.Action<System.Int32> = null, System.Action<AAComm.Extensions.ParamHandlingSummary, System.String> = null)
  Asynchronously writes controller parameters from a .par file (local file -> controller disk). Follows the PCSuite "Parameters Download" convention: reads the .par file, validates parameters against the connected controller, then sends each as a SET command. Ethernet connections use bulk messages (up to 50 per packet); other channels send one by one. After a successful download, optionally sends "ASave" plus per-axis "CalcFilters" to persist parameters to flash. The call is non-blocking; subscribe to the callbacks to be notified of progress and completion.

Class ControllerCommandException (AAMotion; AAMotion C#): A command the controller refused, or answered with a reply the SDK could not read as a value. It is raised by the members that answer with the value itself and so have nowhere to report a failure — the typed properties, GetValue — where a 0 is indistinguishable from the controller genuinely reporting 0. TryRead, TryReadArray and TryGetValue report the same failure as false and never throw. Either way the failed read is recorded in LastReadError and counted by ReadFailures. A typed property set the controller refuses raises it as well, with Command carrying the assignment exactly as sent (ASpeed=1000) — a dropped write leaves the next read answering the old value, with nothing at the call site to say so. A failed write is deliberately not recorded in LastReadError and not counted by ReadFailures: both are the read record, by name and by their own contract, so a consumer reading them keeps being told about reads and nothing else. There is no TrySet — catch this, or subscribe to ErrorOccurred, which is raised for the refusal as before.

Class FastReadCache (AAMotion; AAMotion C#): Fast read cache for high-performance data reading. A background thread refreshes the registered parameters every RefreshIntervalMs, and a read of a registered parameter answers from the last refresh without a controller round trip. Reads never take a lock, so callers polling a value from several threads never hold off the refresh that writes it. A value that was never refreshed, that the controller answered with an error, or that is not a number is a miss: the read goes to the controller instead. A refresh reads supported registrations in channel-sized batches, with motion status last. After a motion begins on an axis (Begin, which every MoveAbs sends), a second thread reads that axis's InTargetStat every InTargetStatRefreshIntervalMs until it reads 4. Until a reading shows the motion has started, the cache does not answer that axis's MotionStat or InTargetStat — those reads go to the controller — for at most MoveStartConfirmMs.

- method AAMotion.ConnectionProbeResult ProbeConnection(System.Nullable<System.Int32> = null)
  Sends one command to the controller and waits for its reply, to tell whether the controller is answering right now — the same path every read and write takes. The command reads Time (seconds since power-on) live, never through the fast read cache, and works on every channel: Ethernet, serial, CAN and simulation. Use it from a dedicated thread, as a heartbeat or before deciding to reconnect. Unlike IsConnected, which only reports whether the SDK still holds the connection, and CheckConnection, which pings the network address, this proves the controller itself answers, says why it did not, and notices a controller restart. A timeout on the wire tears the connection down, as any command timeout does: the server closes the controller's channel for every client on it. Keep timeoutMs above the longest reply the controller can take while busy. A probe that times out still queued behind other commands was never sent and leaves the connection up; IsConnected tells the two apart. The probe never reconnects: when it reports the link down, call TryReconnect on Ethernet, or Disconnect and ConnectSimulation on a simulation. A probe that is sent and fails raises ErrorOccurred and ErrorReported like any other command; one refused because the link is already down raises neither. Concurrent probes on one controller run one at a time.

Class ParameterTypeConverter (AAMotion; AAMotion C#): Parameter type converter - handles type conversion for controller parameters. Core functionality: - The value slot is a Double and holds the parameter's value as the caller sees it, including any User Units scaling AAComm has applied to the reply - Replies are read as decimal numbers and writes are rendered back with the same invariant wire text, so a scaled integral parameter keeps its fraction in both directions - A write carries the display value whole; AAComm's transmit seam divides it by the User Units factor and rounds a firmware-integral parameter in controller counts, so rounding happens once, below the scaling, on every transport - long: read with a separate command rather than from the slot; the controller's 64-bit parameters stay inside +/-2^51, which a double holds exactly - Type detection comes from XML metadata or the cache; use ToInt32Register for bit arithmetic on a register-shaped parameter
Signature: class AAMotion.ParameterTypeConverter

Members:
- method static System.Double ConvertStringToRawValue(AAMotion.eKeyword, System.String)
  Convert a controller reply to the internal value representation. Every reply is read as a decimal number: AAComm hands back the User-Units product of an integral parameter without rounding, so an integer-only parse turns a scaled reply into 0. A reply that is not a finite number resolves to 0 — it has no numeric meaning, and the frameworks disagree both on whether an overflowing literal parses at all and on what a non-finite double narrows to.

  The controller's 32-bit two's-complement view of a slot value, for bit arithmetic on a register-shaped parameter such as a digital-output port or a status word. Function family aamotion_initialize (aamotion.h; AAMotion C).
Signature: aamotion_initialize*

Functions:
- aamotion_controller aamotion_initialize(aamotion_controller_type_t controllerType)
  Creates a session for one controller of the given type and makes sure the shared AACommServer is running. May block a few seconds while the server starts; if the server can never start (missing sidecar, blocked port) the internal retries can block for MINUTES, so call it off any latency-sensitive thread. @param controllerType The controller model; an aamotion_controller_type_t value. @return The session handle, or NULL for an unknown controllerType or when the server could not be started or reached. A non-NULL handle means the server is up, so a later aamotion_connect failure is a connection problem, not an environment one.

Signature: aamotion_open*

Functions:
- bool aamotion_open_aacomm_server(const char* serverExePath)
  Starts AACommServer unless it is already serving its port. Every call checks the port, so a server that exited after an earlier call is started again. @param serverExePath Full path to the server executable, or NULL for the default location. @return true when the server is serving its port. With NULL the default start cannot report a failure, so false then means only that the call itself failed.

Signature: aamotion_connect*

Functions:
- bool aamotion_connect(aamotion_controller controller, const char* deviceAddress, bool fastArk, bool enableAutoReconnect)
  ========================================= Connection ========================================= Connects the session to a controller over Ethernet, serial or CAN. @param deviceAddress The controller's address, e.g. "172.1.1.101". @param fastArk Fast acknowledge mode. @param enableAutoReconnect Recorded but currently has no effect: nothing reconnects on its own; call aamotion_try_reconnect. @return true when connected.
- bool aamotion_connect_simulation(aamotion_controller controller, const char* simExePath, const char* simProduct, const char* simVersion, const char* simMotorProfile)
  Connects the session to a locally spawned firmware simulation instead of a real controller. AACommServer must already be up. To reopen a simulation, call aamotion_disconnect (which frees the handle), then a NEW aamotion_initialize, then this; not aamotion_try_reconnect, and not this alone on an open link, where it returns false. @param simExePath Absolute path to firmware_sim.exe (REQUIRED; the SDK does not ship it). A relative path returns false, since the server starts the simulator from its own directory. @param simProduct Optional product name (NULL = default). A catalogued name such as "AGM800" also declares the controller type, and a simulator that reports another type returns false. @param simVersion Optional firmware version (NULL = default). @param simMotorProfile Optional motor profile (NULL = default).

- bool aamotion_check_connection(aamotion_controller controller)
  Pings the connected controller (ICMP), blocking up to about one second. A link with no IP address (simulation, serial, CAN) is not pinged and reports its logical state. Never disconnects or reconnects. @return false when not connected or not answering.

Signature: aamotion_probe*

Functions:
- bool aamotion_probe_connection(aamotion_controller controller, int timeoutMs, int* failure, double* roundTripMs, long long* controllerTime, bool* controllerRestarted, char* message, int messageSize)
  Sends one command (a live read of the controller's Time) and waits for the reply, to tell whether the controller is answering right now on any channel. A timeout on a command that reached the controller tears the connection down, like any command timeout. @param timeoutMs 0 for the default timeout, else 10..60000. @param failure Receives an aamotion_connection_probe_failure_t; NONE when the controller answered. Required. @param roundTripMs Optional (may be NULL): milliseconds from the call to the reply or failure, 0 when the link was down and nothing was sent. @param controllerTime Optional: the controller's Time (seconds since power-on), -1 without a reply. @param controllerRestarted Optional: true when that Time is lower than at the previous successful probe on this connection, so the controller restarted in between. @param message Optional: the error text when the probe failed, empty when it succeeded. @return true when the probe ran (read *failure for the outcome); false, nothing written, for a bad handle or timeoutMs or a NULL failure.

- typedef void (*aamotion_error_occurred_cb)(int errorCode, const char* message, const char* exception, void* user)
  ============================= Errors, callbacks and descriptions ============================= The error callback fires on whichever thread raised the error: a controller ERR answering your command fires it on YOUR thread, synchronously, inside that call, once per refused write. Keep callbacks short, re-entrancy-safe and thread-safe. Neither a clear_* call nor aamotion_release waits for a callback already running on another thread, so free what a callback uses only once it has returned. Every char* a callback receives is valid only during the call. Receives each error: its code (the n of a controller "ERR n"; errors raised inside the SDK carry their own codes, mostly -1), the command that was sent, and the error text. Each callback receives the registered user pointer. Keep it valid until in-flight calls return.
